/images/memory/memory-art/.webp.caption: Matteo Ricci in the dress of a Chinese scholar, a woodcut portrait from a Chinese account of his life, 17th century. Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.

/images/memory/memory-art/art-of-memory-.caption: A memory theatre from Robert Fludd's art of memory, an engraving from his history of the two worlds (this copy dated 1621). Wellcome Collection. CC BY 4.0, Wikimedia Commons.

/images/memory/memory-art/atrio-tuscanic.caption: The atrium of the Villa Poppaea at Oplontis, with painted walls and the sunken impluvium in the floor. Photograph by Miguel Hermoso Cuesta, 2013. CC BY-SA 4.0, Wikimedia Commons.

/images/memory/memory-art/rhetorica-ad-h.caption: The opening of the Rhetorica ad Herennium in a manuscript copied between 1350 and 1400, with readers' notes in the margins. Beinecke MS 681. Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.

/images/memory/memory-images/rhetorica-a.caption: Opening page of the Rhetorica ad Herennium in a 14th-century manuscript, Vaticanus Palatinus lat. 1459, fol. 1r, Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana. Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.

/images/memory/memory-mind/ebbinghaus.we.caption: Hermann Ebbinghaus, who measured his own forgetting in 1879–80. Photograph by Marie Müller, from the collections of the Humboldt University of Berlin. Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.

/images/memory/memory-numbers/mark-twain.caption: Mark Twain, photographed by A. F. Bradley in New York in 1907. Public domain, Wikimedia Commons.
